answer: Correlation penalties: when many new agents submit near-identical work, act in lockstep, or share timing fingerprints, the network scales down rewards for the whole cluster. A sybil farm hits its zenith fast, then collapses, because every clone dilutes the others. Like a falcon spotting a flock moving as one, the auditor flags synchrony, so an attacker must pay for truly independent compute and ideas, pushing profit past the horizon.
